description: Foundation platform services: the infrastructure layer consumed by all domain and cross-cutting services. Foundation services have no capability_mapping to a business capability — they are platform concerns. Each is a buy candidate; the bank does not build competitive advantage in foundational infrastructure.

services.name: Identity & Access Management
services.description: The authoritative platform service for digital identity, authentication, and authorisation across all bank systems and channels. Provides: customer authentication (biometric, SCA-compliant 2FA under PSD2 RTS), employee and service account identity, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC token issuance for API access, role-based and attribute-based access control (RBAC/ABAC) for internal systems and SM&CR role assignments, TPP (Third Party Provider) certificate validation for Open Banking, and single sign-on (SSO) across internal banking applications. SCA compliance and the bank's digital identity posture are owned here.

dependencies.rationale: All authentication events, access grants, and denial decisions are immutably logged for SM&CR compliance, fraud investigation, and FCA operational resilience evidence.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — customer credential data, employee identity records
regulatory_data_obligations: PSD2 RTS SCA compliance records
SM&CR role assignment records
UK GDPR authentication data
CMA Open Banking TPP certificate validation records
FCA operational resilience impact tolerance (authentication as important business service component)

market_context.build_rationale: IAM is a commodity infrastructure capability with specialist vendors that provide enterprise-grade SCA compliance, TPP certificate management, and OIDC standards support that would take years to build in-house. The bank owns the access policy and SM&CR role assignments; the platform provides the enforcement engine.

vendor_options.notes: UK financial services market leader for customer IAM and Open Banking TPP validation. Used by multiple CMA9 banks for OBIE API access management.
Strong for developer-friendly OIDC/OAuth 2.0 implementation. Auth0 acquisition gives good support for financial services SCA requirements.
Native AWS IAM for cloud-native deployments on AWS. Lower vendor lock-in risk if bank is predominantly AWS-hosted.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-100 implements UK Digital Identity and Attributes Trust Framework (DIATF) certified identity verification for new customer onboarding journeys alongside traditional eKYC.
design_decisions.rationale: DSIT's DIATF (Data (Use and Access) Act 2025) creates a certified digital identity ecosystem. Banks that accept DIATF-certified identity proofs at onboarding reduce friction while meeting MLR 2017 CDD obligations. SVC-100 acts as the DIATF relying party; certified identity providers (e.g. Yoti, Onfido-certified schemes) present identity claims to SVC-100 which validates the DIATF certificate before passing the identity assertion to SVC-050 (Customer Onboarding).
alternatives_considered: Build proprietary identity verification without DIATF integration
design_decisions.rejected_because: DIATF is the UK government's strategic digital identity infrastructure. Early adoption reduces onboarding friction and positions the bank as a digital identity relying party rather than a laggard.

services.name: API Gateway
services.description: The authoritative platform service for external and internal API management. Provides: inbound API rate limiting and throttling (protection against Open Banking API abuse), TLS termination and certificate management, API versioning and routing, TPP certificate validation for Open Banking FAPI compliance, consumer (mobile app, TPP, corporate ERP) authentication and authorisation delegation (token validation), API product catalogue, usage analytics and quota management, developer portal for fintech partners, and API monitoring with SLA alerting. Sits at the edge of all external-facing API surfaces: Open Banking APIs, corporate banking APIs, and internal service-to-service calls crossing security domains.

dependencies.rationale: Token validation and TPP certificate verification delegate to SVC-100. API Gateway enforces access policy defined by IAM.
All inbound API calls, rate limit breaches, and authentication failures are logged for CMA Open Banking performance reporting, FCA supervisory inspection, and security incident investigation.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK — API call metadata and analytics
regulatory_data_obligations: CMA Order Open Banking API performance reporting
OBIE API availability and incident records
FCA operational resilience important business service boundary monitoring

market_context.build_rationale: API gateway is infrastructure commodity. CAP-007 build_vs_buy identifies Apigee or AWS API Gateway as buy candidates. The bank's differentiation is in the API products (Open Banking, corporate banking) not the gateway infrastructure.

vendor_options.notes: Enterprise API management with strong Open Banking and FAPI support. API product catalogue, developer portal, analytics. Used by several UK banks for Open Banking compliance.
Native AWS API management. Lower operational overhead if bank is predominantly AWS-hosted. Strong for serverless and microservice architectures.
Open-source API gateway with enterprise support. Cloud-agnostic. Strong plugin ecosystem for rate limiting, auth, and logging.

services.name: Event Bus
services.description: The authoritative platform service for asynchronous, durable event streaming across all bank services. Provides: publish-subscribe event delivery with guaranteed delivery semantics, event schema registry and schema evolution management, event sourcing support for domain event logs, consumer group management and offset tracking, dead letter queue handling for failed event processing, and cross-domain event routing. The event bus is the primary integration mechanism between domain services — it replaces point-to-point synchronous calls for non-blocking communication and enables event-driven architecture patterns (event sourcing, CQRS, saga orchestration).

dependencies.rationale: Event publication and consumption events are logged for audit trail, regulatory replay capability, and operational debugging.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — financial events may contain customer PII and transaction data
regulatory_data_obligations: Financial event replay capability for PRA supervisory investigation
UK GDPR personal data in event payloads (data minimisation required)
FCA operational resilience event pipeline availability requirements

market_context.build_rationale: Event streaming infrastructure is commodity. Apache Kafka (Confluent managed service) or AWS Kinesis are proven at financial services scale. Building event streaming infrastructure in-house is not justified — the bank competes on the events it produces and the services that consume them, not on the message broker.

vendor_options.notes: Managed Apache Kafka with schema registry, RBAC, audit logging. Used at financial services scale. UK-hosted cloud option. Strong operational tooling.
AWS-native event streaming. Lower operational overhead if bank is AWS-hosted. MSK (Managed Kafka) for Kafka compatibility.

design_decisions.decision: All domain events must be published with a schema version and must be backward-compatible for a minimum of two versions. Breaking schema changes require a new event type.
design_decisions.rationale: Domain services are deployed independently. A schema change in a producing service must not break consuming services that have not yet been updated. Financial events (PaymentSettled, LoanOriginated) may need to be replayed for regulatory investigation — the schema must support historical replay without data loss.
alternatives_considered: No schema versioning; consumer and producer deploy simultaneously
design_decisions.rejected_because: Coordinated deployment of all services is operationally impractical at scale and eliminates the independent deployability that is the primary benefit of event-driven architecture.

services.name: Audit & Logging
services.description: The authoritative platform service for immutable audit logging, security event management, and compliance evidence across all bank systems. Provides: immutable append-only audit log storage (tamper-evident, cryptographically sealed), security information and event management (SIEM) with real-time correlation and alerting, structured log aggregation across all services, log retention policy enforcement aligned to regulatory requirements (minimum 5 years for AML records; 7 years for financial records), and audit query API for compliance investigations and FCA supervisory data requests. Supports SM&CR individual accountability evidence, Consumer Duty outcomes monitoring, and FCA/PRA supervisory data delivery.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — audit logs contain PII, financial transaction data, and MLRO-protected SAR metadata
regulatory_data_obligations: MLR 2017 five-year minimum audit record retention
PRA seven-year financial records retention
SM&CR individual conduct evidence trail
FCA operational resilience incident evidence
PCI DSS cardholder data access log retention
UK GDPR processing activity records (ROPA inputs)

market_context.build_rationale: Audit logging and SIEM are infrastructure commodities with specialist vendors that provide regulatory-grade immutability guarantees, compliance reporting, and 24/7 security operations support. Building bespoke audit infrastructure risks compliance gaps; specialist platforms maintain regulatory content and detection rule libraries.

vendor_options.notes: Dominant SIEM in UK financial services. Pre-built compliance dashboards for PCI DSS, SOX, GDPR. Real-time correlation, threat hunting. FCA operational resilience incident reporting support.
Cloud-native SIEM/SOAR. Strong if bank is Azure-hosted. Cost model (consumption-based) competitive at scale.
AWS-native immutable audit trail and security event management. Lower overhead if bank is AWS-hosted.

services.name: Data Platform
services.description: The authoritative platform service for enterprise data aggregation, analytics, and ML model serving. Provides: data lake and data warehouse capabilities for cross-domain analytical queries, feature store for ML model inputs (fraud detection, credit scoring, AML transaction monitoring), data cataloguing and lineage tracking (UK GDPR ROPA support, PRA data quality supervision), regulatory reporting data aggregation (COREP, FINREP, PRA statistical returns), customer data product for Consumer Duty outcomes analytics, and API-accessible data services for approved consumers. Implements the bank's data governance framework including data quality rules, PII classification, and retention enforcement.

dependencies.rationale: Domain events from all services are streamed into the data platform via the event bus. This is the primary ingestion mechanism — the data platform does not query operational databases directly.
Data access and data query events are logged for UK GDPR ROPA obligations and PRA data quality audit.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — consolidated customer and financial data
regulatory_data_obligations: UK GDPR data minimisation and purpose limitation in analytical processing
PRA data quality supervision requirements
FCA Consumer Duty outcomes analytics data
FSCS eligibility data aggregation
COREP/FINREP regulatory return data derivation
PRA SS1/23 model data lineage requirements

market_context.build_rationale: Data platform infrastructure (data lake, data warehouse, feature store) is a well-established cloud commodity. Cloud-native data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, AWS Redshift) provide the scale, governance, and ML integration that would take years to build in-house. The bank owns the data products, data models, and governance policies; the platform provides the infrastructure.

vendor_options.notes: Unified data + ML platform. Delta Lake for ACID-compliant data lake. MLflow for model lifecycle management. Strong for feature store (SVC-013 fraud ML, SVC-052 credit ML, SVC-014 AML ML). Growing UK FS adoption.
Cloud-native data warehouse. Strong governance and data sharing capabilities. Less integrated ML tooling than Databricks.
AWS-native data warehouse and ML platform. Strong integration with other AWS services. Preferred if bank is AWS-native.

design_decisions.decision: The data platform is the only system permitted to query across domain service data for analytics. Domain services do not query each other's operational databases directly.
design_decisions.rationale: Direct cross-domain database queries create tight operational coupling, violate bounded context boundaries, and create race conditions between analytical queries and operational transactions. The event stream provides an eventually consistent analytical replica in the data platform, which is the correct integration point for analytics. This pattern enables domain services to evolve their data schemas independently.
alternatives_considered: Allow direct cross-service database queries for regulatory reporting
design_decisions.rejected_because: Cross-service database queries create schema coupling and would prevent independent service evolution. Regulatory reporting latency (daily batch) is compatible with event-driven data platform ingestion.

services.name: Secrets Management
services.description: The authoritative platform service for storing, rotating, and auditing access to cryptographic keys, API credentials, database passwords, certificates, and other sensitive configuration. Provides: hardware security module (HSM) backed key storage, automatic secrets rotation without service downtime, dynamic secrets (short-lived credentials generated on-demand for database access), secrets access policies tied to SVC-100 service identities, and full audit trail of every secret access event. Prevents hard-coded credentials in application code or configuration files across all services. Critical for PCI DSS key management requirements and GDPR encryption obligations.

dependencies.rationale: Service identity (machine identity) is verified via SVC-100 before any secret is granted. Only authenticated service accounts with the correct IAM role receive secrets.
Every secret access event is logged immutably for PCI DSS key management audit and security incident investigation.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — cryptographic key material must not leave UK jurisdiction
regulatory_data_obligations: PCI DSS key management and HSM requirements
UK GDPR encryption key management for personal data at rest
FCA operational resilience cryptographic key availability requirements
PRA DORA-equivalent ICT security key management controls

market_context.build_rationale: Secrets management is a security infrastructure commodity. HashiCorp Vault (now owned by IBM) and cloud-native secrets managers (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault) provide HSM-backed key storage, automatic rotation, and dynamic secrets at PCI DSS grade. Building a proprietary secrets vault is not justified and creates security risk from undiscovered implementation flaws.

vendor_options.notes: Industry-standard secrets management. HSM integration, dynamic secrets, fine-grained access policies. Widely deployed in UK financial services. Cloud-agnostic.
AWS-native secrets management with HSM-backed key storage (CloudHSM). Lower operational overhead if AWS-native deployment.

services.name: Service Mesh
services.description: The authoritative platform service providing secure, observable, and resilient service-to-service communication for all internal microservices. Provides: mutual TLS (mTLS) for all service-to-service calls (zero-trust network model), traffic management (load balancing, circuit breaking, retry policies, timeouts), service discovery and health checking, distributed tracing for end-to-end request observability across service boundaries, security policy enforcement (which services are permitted to call which other services), and rate limiting for internal API calls. Transparent to application code — implemented as a sidecar proxy (Envoy-based) injected alongside each service container.

dependencies.rationale: Service mesh identity certificates (SPIFFE/SPIRE) are issued by or coordinated with the bank's PKI in SVC-100.
Distributed traces and service-to-service call metrics are exported to SVC-103 for operational monitoring and FCA operational resilience important business service mapping.

technology_constraints.data_residency: N/A — service mesh operates at the infrastructure layer; it does not store application data
regulatory_data_obligations: FCA operational resilience service dependency mapping (SS1/21 important business service decomposition)
PRA DORA-equivalent ICT network security controls (mTLS, zero trust)
PCI DSS network segmentation evidence (service mesh enforces segment boundaries)

market_context.build_rationale: Service mesh is platform infrastructure commodity. Istio and Linkerd are open-source projects maintained by CNCF with cloud-managed variants (GKE, EKS). Building a bespoke service mesh is not appropriate — this is a solved infrastructure problem.

vendor_options.notes: CNCF graduated project. Envoy-based sidecar proxy. Strong policy, observability, and mTLS. Widely adopted in financial services. Managed variant available on GKE (Anthos Service Mesh).
Simpler alternative to Istio. Lower operational overhead. CNCF graduated. Rust-based proxy with minimal latency overhead.

design_decisions.decision: The service mesh enforces explicit allow-list policies for all service-to-service calls. Services that are not explicitly permitted to communicate are blocked by default (deny-all baseline).
design_decisions.rationale: The PCI DSS cardholder data environment (CDE) boundary requires demonstrable network segmentation between CDE-scoped services (SVC-003, SVC-008, SVC-011) and non-CDE services. The service mesh explicit allow-list policy provides this segmentation at the application network layer, supporting PCI DSS audit evidence. The FCA operational resilience important business service decomposition also benefits from the service mesh dependency map.
alternatives_considered: Allow-all baseline with explicit deny policies for sensitive services
design_decisions.rejected_because: Allow-all baseline creates an insecure default where new services can freely call sensitive financial services. PCI DSS requires demonstrable segmentation; deny-all with explicit allow-list is the only defensible posture.
